system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

For every objection also fill `uae_basis`: if one of the UAE clauses shown (ids starting with ITU-UAE:, TDRA-,
UAE-, DXB-) speaks to this issue, set status "cites_uae" with its id and a word-for-word quote; otherwise set
status "none_applies" with empty ref and quote. Say "none_applies" honestly: it tells the regulator where UAE
texts are silent.

Structure of the CAP alert message Each CAP alert message consists of an <alert> segment, which may contain one or more <info> segments, each of which may include one or more <area> and/or <resource> segments. Under most circumstances, CAP messages with a <msgType> value of "Alert" should include at least one <info> element. (See the document object model diagram in clause 7.1, below). • <alert> The <alert> segment provides basic information about the current message: its purpose, its source and its status, as well as a unique identifier for the current message and links to any other, related messages. An <alert> segment may be used alone for message acknowledgements, cancellations or other system functions, but most <alert> segments will include at least one <info> segment. • <info> The <info> segment describes an anticipated or actual event in terms of its urgency (time available to prepare), severity (intensity of impact) and certainty (confidence in the observation or prediction), as well as providing both categorical and textual descriptions of the subject event. It may also provide instructions for appropriate response by message recipients and various other details (hazard duration, technical parameters, contact information, links to additional information sources, etc.).

data.summary: The alert does not match the verified bulletin. Description is 'unknown', so the hazard, place and end time are missing. The instruction gives no area or duration. Certainty 'Likely' is lower than the bulletin supports for a shelter order already in effect, and the timing conflict (10 pm vs 10:30 pm) is not stated.

objections.issue: Description is the placeholder 'unknown'. The alert never states the hazard (police activity, possible armed domestic situation), the place (3600 block of West Broadway, Robbinsdale; 3600-3700 block of Hubbard and West Broadway) or the time. The headline is also generic.
objections.fix: Replace the description with the verified facts: police activity involving a possible armed domestic situation in the 3600 block of West Broadway, Robbinsdale; three people detained and information on additional suspects. Name the affected blocks (3600-3700 Hubbard and West Broadway).
